recipes.title: Watermelon and feta salad with Aleppo pepper and mint
recipes.why: Red fruit meets red fruit; the Aleppo pepper's warmth asks for a rosé with a little spice behind it.
steps: Soak the red onion in the lime juice for 10 minutes so it softens and turns pink.
Chill the watermelon chunks while the onion soaks.
Arrange the watermelon on a platter and crumble the feta over it in large pieces.
Scatter the onion over the top and spoon on the lime juice, then drizzle with the olive oil.
Finish with the Aleppo pepper, torn mint and a pinch of flaky salt. Serve at once.

recipes.title: Beetroot tartare with hazelnuts and sour cherries
recipes.why: The sour cherries pull it toward a juicy, bright red; earthy beet and toasted hazelnut sit well with light tannin.
steps: Wrap the beetroot in foil and roast at 200 °C for about 1 hour, until a knife slides in easily.
Let the beetroot cool, rub off the skins and cut into 5 mm dice.
Whisk the sherry vinegar, Dijon mustard and olive oil, then fold in the beetroot, shallot, capers, sour cherries and thyme. Season with salt.
Rest for 10 minutes so the cherries plump in the dressing.
Press into rings on plates, top with the hazelnuts and serve with the toasted sourdough.

recipes.title: Carrot salad with orange blossom, toasted cumin and pistachios
recipes.why: Orange blossom matches an aromatic, floral white; the cumin adds a warm edge without needing tannin.
steps: Toast the cumin seeds in a dry pan for about 2 minutes, until fragrant, then crush lightly.
Whisk the orange zest and juice, lemon juice, honey, orange blossom water and olive oil with a pinch of salt.
Toss the carrots with the dressing and half the cumin. Leave for 10 minutes.
Pile onto a plate and finish with the pistachios, coriander leaves and the rest of the cumin.

recipes.title: Green asparagus with soft egg and white pepper gremolata
recipes.why: White pepper is the signature of a peppery, crisp white; the acidity handles both asparagus and yolk.
steps: Mix the parsley, lemon zest, garlic and white pepper with a pinch of salt to make the gremolata.
Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 6½ minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.
Blanch the asparagus in salted boiling water for 2–3 minutes, until just tender, and drain.
Dress the asparagus with the olive oil and lemon juice and lay it on plates.
Halve the eggs over the asparagus, scatter with the gremolata and parmesan.

recipes.title: Leeks vinaigrette with chopped egg and verjuice
recipes.why: Verjuice gives a soft, green sourness that wants a lean, high-acid white with little fruit.
steps: Simmer the leeks whole in salted water for 12–15 minutes, until a knife meets no resistance.
Drain the leeks and press gently in a clean towel to remove the water.
Whisk the verjuice, Dijon mustard and shallot, then whisk in the olive oil. Season.
Split the leeks lengthwise and spoon the dressing over them while still warm.
Grate the eggs over the top and finish with the capers and chives.

recipes.title: Seared scallops with green apple, celeriac and lemon verbena
recipes.why: Lemon verbena oil lifts the plate toward a floral, racy white; the apple echoes its green fruit.
steps: Warm the olive oil with the lemon verbena leaves to 60 °C, then leave off the heat for 20 minutes and strain.
Simmer the celeriac in the milk with a pinch of salt for about 20 minutes, until soft, then blend with the butter until smooth.
Toss the green apple with half the lime juice.
Sear the scallops in a very hot pan with a little oil, 90 seconds per side, and finish with the rest of the lime juice.
Spoon the purée onto plates, add the scallops and apple and drizzle with the verbena oil.

recipes.title: Roast cod with miso brown butter and toasted buckwheat
recipes.why: Toasted buckwheat and brown butter mirror the toast of an oaked white; the miso gives it savoury depth.
steps: Toss the cauliflower in the olive oil and salt and roast at 220 °C for 20–25 minutes, until well coloured.
Season the cod and roast skin-side up alongside for the last 10–12 minutes.
Cook the butter in a small pan until it foams and smells nutty, add the toasted buckwheat for 1 minute, then take it off the heat and whisk in the white miso and lemon juice.
Plate the cauliflower and cod and spoon over the miso brown butter with its crunchy buckwheat.

recipes.title: Monkfish with saffron, fennel and orange
recipes.why: Saffron adds a floral note a round white can follow; orange and fennel keep it fresh.
steps: Toss the fennel with the garlic, olive oil and salt and roast at 200 °C for 15 minutes.
Pour the white wine, orange juice and saffron water over the fennel.
Season the monkfish, add it to the dish and roast for 12–15 minutes more, until just firm.
Spoon the pan juices over the fish and finish with the orange zest and fennel fronds.

recipes.title: Sea bass ceviche with passion fruit and pink peppercorns
recipes.why: Passion fruit pushes the dish toward an aromatic white with tropical fruit; the lime needs its acidity.

ingredients.name: sea bass
ingredients.note: very fresh, skinned, in 1.5 cm dice

steps: Chill the sea bass and a bowl for 10 minutes.
Mix the lime juice, passion fruit pulp and red chilli with a good pinch of salt.
Pour over the fish, toss and leave for 4–5 minutes, until the edges turn opaque.
Spoon into chilled bowls with the juice and top with the red onion, coriander leaves and pink peppercorns.

recipes.title: Rack of lamb with a coffee and cocoa nib crust
recipes.why: Coffee and cocoa echo the toast of a structured, oaked red; lamb fat softens its tannin.
steps: Toss the potatoes with half the olive oil and salt and roast at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Mix the ground coffee, cocoa nibs, breadcrumbs, rosemary, garlic, black pepper and the rest of the oil.
Season the lamb, sear it fat-side down until golden, then brush with the Dijon mustard and press on the crust.
Add the lamb to the potato tray and roast for 18–22 minutes for pink meat.
Rest for 10 minutes before carving into cutlets.

recipes.title: Grilled ribeye with bone marrow butter and juniper
recipes.why: Fat and char tame a very tannic red; juniper picks up its dark, resinous spice.
steps: Roast the bone marrow at 220 °C for 15 minutes, then scoop out the marrow and let it cool.
Mash the marrow with the butter, juniper berries, shallot and parsley and chill.
Season the steaks with black pepper and grill over high heat, 4–5 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Rest for 8 minutes, then slice and top with spoonfuls of the marrow butter and flaky salt.

recipes.title: Venison loin with blackberries and star anise
recipes.why: Star anise and blackberry follow a spicy, ripe red with some oak; lean venison needs its body.
steps: Roast the parsnips with the olive oil and salt at 200 °C for 30 minutes.
Sweat the shallot in half the butter, add the red wine and star anise and reduce by half.
Add the beef stock and reduce until syrupy, then remove the star anise and add the blackberries for 1 minute.
Season the venison and sear in the rest of the butter for 3 minutes per side, then roast for 6 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes, slice and serve with the parsnips and the blackberry sauce.

recipes.title: Chicken thighs with roasted red grapes and lavender honey
recipes.why: Lavender and roasted grapes bring out the floral, juicy side of a light red; the chicken keeps tannin low.
steps: Warm the honey with the dried lavender, then stir in the red wine vinegar.
Season the chicken thighs and lay them skin-side up in a tray with the onion, garlic and thyme. Drizzle with the olive oil.
Roast at 210 °C for 20 minutes.
Add the red grapes, brush everything with the lavender honey and roast for 15–20 minutes more, until the skin is crisp.
Spoon the pan juices over before serving.

recipes.title: Duck breast with sour cherries and Sichuan pepper
recipes.why: Sichuan pepper adds a tingling spice a supple, fresh red can match; the cherries need its acidity.
steps: Season the duck breasts and place skin-side down in a cold pan. Cook over medium heat for 10–12 minutes to render the fat.
Turn and cook for 3 minutes more, then rest skin-side up for 8 minutes.
Sear the red chicory cut-side down in a little duck fat until caramelised.
In the same pan, soften the shallot, add the red wine, sour cherries and honey and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the butter and the Sichuan peppercorns.
Slice the duck and serve with the chicory and the cherry sauce.

recipes.title: Slow-roast pork shoulder with figs and black olives
recipes.why: Dried figs pull the dish toward a ripe, fruit-forward red; salty olives balance the sweetness.
steps: Rub the pork with the fennel seeds, salt and olive oil and brown it all over in a casserole.
Lift the pork out, soften the onion and garlic in the fat, then add the red wine and bay leaves.
Return the pork, cover and cook at 160 °C for 2½ hours.
Add the dried figs and black olives and cook uncovered for 45 minutes more, until the meat pulls apart.
Slice or pull the pork and serve with the figs, olives and juices.

recipes.title: Aubergine parmigiana with smoked scamorza
recipes.why: Tomato needs a high-acid red; the smoked scamorza adds a smoky depth that its savoury tannin can meet.
steps: Salt the aubergines for 20 minutes, pat dry and fry in batches in the olive oil until golden on both sides.
Simmer the passata with the garlic, dried oregano and half the basil for 15 minutes. Season.
Layer sauce, aubergines, smoked scamorza and parmesan in a baking dish, finishing with sauce and parmesan.
Bake at 190 °C for 30–35 minutes, until bubbling and browned.
Rest for 15 minutes and serve with the rest of the basil.

recipes.title: Puy lentil and mushroom ragù with clove and orange zest
recipes.why: Clove and porcini call for a spicy, fruity red; the lentils give it enough weight for gentle tannin.
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the olive oil for 10 minutes.
Add the chestnut mushrooms and cook until browned, then stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the red wine, the chopped porcini and their soaking water (leaving any grit behind), the lentils, cloves and bay leaves.
Simmer for 30–35 minutes, adding water as needed, until the lentils are tender. Remove the cloves and bay.
Cook the polenta according to the packet, spoon the ragù on top and finish with the orange zest.

recipes.title: Crisp polenta chips with lemon salt and fennel pollen
recipes.why: Fried and salty is the classic match for a sparkling wine; fennel pollen adds a floral lift.
steps: Bring the water to a boil with salt, whisk in the polenta and cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
Beat in the parmesan and butter, spread 2 cm thick in a lined tray and chill until firm, at least 1 hour.
Rub the lemon zest into the flaky salt and fennel pollen.
Cut the polenta into thick chips and fry in the sunflower oil at 180 °C until crisp and golden.
Drain and toss at once with the lemon salt.

recipes.title: Smoked trout rillettes with horseradish on rye
recipes.why: Smoked fish meets an oaked white; horseradish adds a sharp spice its creamy texture can carry.
steps: Beat the butter and creme fraiche until smooth.
Fold in the smoked trout, horseradish, lemon zest and juice, and half the dill. Season with black pepper.
Chill for 30 minutes to firm up.
Spread thickly on the rye bread and top with the capers, chives and the rest of the dill.

recipes.title: Cabrales with toasted walnuts and date syrup
recipes.why: Salty blue cheese needs a very sweet, dense wine; date syrup builds a bridge to its dried-fruit richness.
steps: Toast the walnuts at 180 °C for 6–8 minutes and let them cool.
Set the cabrales on a board with the pear slices and oat crackers.
Scatter the walnuts over the cheese and drizzle with the date syrup just before serving.

recipes.title: Aged Gouda with smoked almonds and quince paste
recipes.why: Crystalline aged cheese stands up to firm tannin; smoked almonds echo the oak of a powerful red.
steps: Take the aged gouda out of the fridge 30 minutes before serving.
Arrange the shards on a board with the quince paste and oat crackers.
Scatter the smoked almonds around and grind a little black pepper over the cheese.

recipes.title: Apricot tarte tatin with saffron
recipes.why: Caramel and apricot ask for a sweet wine with more sugar than the tart; saffron adds a floral edge.
steps: Melt the caster sugar in a 24 cm ovenproof pan to a deep amber caramel, then whisk in the butter, saffron and vanilla.
Pack the apricots cut-side up tightly in the caramel and cook for 5 minutes.
Lay the puff pastry over the top, tuck in the edges and prick a few times.
Bake at 200 °C for 25–30 minutes, until the pastry is deep golden.
Rest for 5 minutes, turn out onto a plate and serve warm with the creme fraiche.

recipes.title: Dark chocolate and fig pots with black pepper
recipes.why: Chocolate needs a fortified wine sweeter than itself; black pepper and figs follow its spice and dried fruit.
steps: Heat the double cream, milk and black pepper until steaming, then pour over the dark chocolate and stir until smooth.
Whisk the egg yolks with the caster sugar and sea salt, then whisk in the chocolate cream.
Pour into 6 small ramekins, set in a roasting tin and add hot water halfway up the sides.
Bake at 150 °C for 30–35 minutes, until set at the edges with a slight wobble. Chill for at least 3 hours.
Serve topped with the fresh figs.

recipes.title: Poached white peaches with elderflower and almond crumble
recipes.why: Elderflower and white peach echo a floral, sweet sparkling wine; its sweetness stays above the fruit's.
steps: Rub the butter into the plain flour, ground almonds and 1 tbsp of the sugar, spread on a tray and bake at 180 °C for 12–15 minutes, until golden.
Bring the water, the rest of the caster sugar, the elderflower cordial and lemon juice to a simmer.
Poach the white peaches for 8–10 minutes, turning, until tender. Slip off the skins.
Reduce the poaching liquid by half and let it cool.
Serve the peaches halved with the syrup, a spoonful of greek yoghurt and the crumble.

recipes.title: Roasted pineapple with lime, ginger and Thai basil
recipes.why: Pineapple and lime need a late-harvest wine with high acidity; Thai basil adds a fresh, floral lift.
steps: Mix the light brown sugar, melted butter, fresh ginger and half the lime juice.
Toss the pineapple in the mixture and roast at 220 °C for 20–25 minutes, turning once, until caramelised at the edges.
Splash the rest of the lime juice into the tray to loosen the juices.
Serve warm with the coconut yoghurt, lime zest and torn Thai basil.

recipes.title: Mackerel with rhubarb and pink pepper
recipes.why: Rhubarb's sharpness needs a racy, aromatic white to cut through the oily fish.
steps: Toss the rhubarb with the caster sugar and lemon juice and roast at 200 °C for 8 minutes, until just soft.
Brush the mackerel fillets with olive oil, season and grill skin-side up for 4–5 minutes, until the skin blisters.
Serve the mackerel with the rhubarb and its juices, scattered with the pink peppercorns and dill.

recipes.title: Crab salad with grapefruit and tarragon
recipes.why: Grapefruit and tarragon lift sweet crab toward a floral, high-acid white.
steps: Fold the crab meat with the mayonnaise, lemon juice and half the tarragon. Season.
Arrange the little gem lettuce leaves on plates and spoon the crab into them.
Add the grapefruit segments and finish with the remaining tarragon and chives.

recipes.title: Steamed sea bream with ginger, lime leaf and spring onion
recipes.why: Lime leaf and ginger make it fragrant enough for an aromatic, bone-dry white.
steps: Score the sea bream, stuff with half the ginger and the kaffir lime leaves and steam for 10–12 minutes.
Transfer to a plate, pour over the light soy sauce and top with the rest of the ginger and the spring onions.
Heat the sunflower oil until smoking and pour it over the fish so the aromatics sizzle.

recipes.title: Thai-style prawn salad with green mango and chilli
recipes.why: The chilli heat and sweet-sour dressing call for an off-dry white with bright acidity.
steps: Poach the king prawns in simmering salted water for 2 minutes and cool.
Dissolve the palm sugar in the lime juice and fish sauce, then stir in the red chilli.
Toss the prawns and green mango with the dressing, mint and coriander leaves.
Pile onto plates and scatter with the roasted peanuts.

recipes.title: Hot-smoked salmon with pickled cucumber and yuzu kosho crème fraîche
recipes.why: Yuzu kosho's citrus heat and the sweet pickle want a touch of sweetness and lots of acidity in the glass.
steps: Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar, caster sugar and a pinch of salt and leave for 15 minutes.
Stir the yuzu kosho into the creme fraiche.
Spread the rye bread with the yuzu kosho cream, top with the drained cucumber and hot-smoked salmon and finish with dill.

recipes.title: Grilled sardines with tomato, oregano and lemon
recipes.why: Oily sardines and tomato need a crisp, juicy white with plenty of acidity.
steps: Rub the sardines with olive oil and flaky salt and grill over high heat for 2–3 minutes per side.
Toss the tomatoes and red onion with the rest of the olive oil and the dried oregano.
Serve the sardines on the tomato salad with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Hake with clams, green sauce and Espelette pepper
recipes.why: Parsley, garlic and briny clams match a fresh, fruity white from the Atlantic coast.
steps: Gently fry the garlic in the olive oil in a wide pan without colouring, then stir in the plain flour.
Add the dry white wine and season the hake, then lay it in the pan skin-side up and cook for 4 minutes, shaking the pan.
Add the clams, cover and cook for 3–4 minutes until they open.
Turn the hake, stir in the parsley and shake until the sauce turns green and silky. Dust with the espelette pepper.

recipes.title: Scallop ceviche with nectarine and yuzu
recipes.why: Yuzu and nectarine lift the sweetness of raw scallop toward a juicy, aromatic white.
steps: Arrange the scallops and nectarine slices on chilled plates.
Mix the yuzu juice, lime juice and olive oil and spoon over 5 minutes before serving.
Finish with the shiso leaves and flaky salt.

recipes.title: Fritto misto with lemon and sage
recipes.why: Crisp, salty frying is the classic partner for sparkling wine's bubbles and acidity.
steps: Heat the sunflower oil to 180 °C.
Toss the squid, king prawns, courgette and sage leaves in the seasoned plain flour and shake off the excess.
Fry in small batches for 1–2 minutes, until crisp and pale gold.
Drain, sprinkle with flaky salt and serve at once with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Oysters with shallot and Champagne vinegar mignonette
recipes.why: Briny oysters and sharp vinegar want a bone-dry sparkling with lots of acidity.
steps: Mix the shallot, champagne vinegar and black pepper and leave for 10 minutes.
Set the oysters on crushed ice.
Spoon a little mignonette over each oyster and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Tempura prawns with yuzu salt
recipes.why: Light, crisp batter and citrus salt are made for a dry sparkling.
steps: Rub the yuzu zest into the flaky salt.
Whisk the plain flour and sparkling water briefly into a lumpy batter.
Dip the king prawns and fry in the sunflower oil at 180 °C for 2 minutes.
Drain and serve with the yuzu salt.

recipes.title: Lobster with tarragon butter and new potatoes
recipes.why: Rich lobster and butter need a creamy, oaked white.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Mash the butter with the tarragon, garlic, lemon zest and juice.
Spread the tarragon butter over the lobster halves and grill for 4–5 minutes, until bubbling.
Serve with the potatoes and the pan butter.

recipes.title: Turbot with beurre blanc and smoked leeks
recipes.why: Beurre blanc's richness and the smoke from the leeks match a toasty, oaked white.
steps: Char the leeks cut-side down on a hot grill, then braise them with a splash of water until tender and season with the smoked salt.
Reduce the shallot, dry white wine and white wine vinegar to 2 tablespoons, then whisk in the butter piece by piece.
Poach the turbot in barely simmering salted water for 6–7 minutes.
Serve the turbot on the leeks with the beurre blanc.

recipes.title: Roast hake with chorizo crumbs and butter beans
recipes.why: Smoky paprika and butter beans want a rounder, barrel-aged white.
steps: Fry the chorizo in the olive oil until crisp, then stir in the breadcrumbs until golden.
Warm the butter beans with the garlic and a splash of water.
Roast the hake at 200 °C for 10 minutes, then top with the chorizo crumbs.
Serve on the butter beans with parsley.

recipes.title: Brill with mushrooms, chicken jus and thyme
recipes.why: Earthy mushrooms and a meaty jus make the dish rich enough for a full, oaked white.
steps: Fry the chestnut mushrooms in half the butter with the shallot and thyme until golden.
Add the reduced chicken stock and simmer for 3 minutes.
Sear the brill in the rest of the butter for 2–3 minutes per side.
Serve the fish on the mushrooms and spoon over the jus.

recipes.title: Smoked haddock with leeks and grain mustard sauce
recipes.why: Smoked fish and a creamy sauce suit a white with some oak and a fresh finish.
steps: Boil the potatoes until tender.
Poach the smoked haddock in the milk for 6 minutes, then lift out and keep the milk.
Soften the leeks in the butter, stir in the plain flour, then whisk in the poaching milk to a smooth sauce. Add the wholegrain mustard.
Serve the haddock on the potatoes and leeks with the sauce and chives.

recipes.title: Cod wrapped in speck with lentils and salsa verde
recipes.why: Smoky speck and herbs suit a crisp white with a little oak.
steps: Simmer the puy lentils for 20 minutes until tender and season.
Blitz the parsley, capers, anchovies, lemon juice and olive oil into a salsa verde.
Wrap each cod portion in speck and roast at 200 °C for 12 minutes.
Serve on the lentils with the salsa verde.

recipes.title: Halibut with saffron mussels and fennel
recipes.why: Saffron and shellfish need a round white with gentle aromatics.
steps: Soften the shallot and fennel, add the dry white wine and mussels, cover and cook until they open. Strain and keep the liquor.
Add the saffron and double cream to the liquor and reduce a little.
Poach the halibut in the sauce for 6–7 minutes.
Return the shelled mussels to warm through and serve.

recipes.title: Salmon with sorrel sauce
recipes.why: Sorrel's lemony sharpness and the salmon's richness want a round white with fresh acidity.
steps: Soften the shallot in the butter, add the dry white wine and reduce by half.
Add the double cream, simmer for 2 minutes and stir in the sorrel until it wilts.
Sear the salmon fillets skin-side down for 5 minutes, then turn for 1 minute.
Spoon the sorrel sauce onto plates and set the salmon on top.

recipes.title: Prawns in coconut and lemongrass broth
recipes.why: Coconut and lemongrass need an aromatic, round white without oak.
steps: Simmer the coconut milk with the lemongrass and fresh ginger for 10 minutes.
Add the king prawns and cook for 3 minutes, then season with the fish sauce and lime juice.
Cook the rice noodles, divide into bowls and ladle over the broth. Finish with coriander leaves.

recipes.title: Cod with chickpeas, spinach and preserved lemon
recipes.why: Preserved lemon gives a fragrant tang that suits a medium-bodied white.
steps: Fry the garlic and cumin seeds in the olive oil, add the chickpeas and preserved lemon and warm through.
Stir in the spinach until wilted.
Roast the cod at 200 °C for 10–12 minutes and serve on the chickpeas.

recipes.title: Plaice with brown shrimp, capers and mace
recipes.why: Brown shrimp and capers need a lean, saline white with sharp acidity.
steps: Season the plaice and fry in half the butter for 2 minutes per side. Keep warm.
Add the rest of the butter to the pan and let it foam, then add the brown shrimp, capers and ground mace.
Add the lemon juice and parsley and spoon over the fish.

recipes.title: Moules marinière with celery leaf
recipes.why: Mussels, garlic and wine are the classic for a bone-dry, saline white.
steps: Soften the shallot and garlic in the butter in a large pot.
Add the mussels and dry white wine, cover and cook for 4–5 minutes, shaking, until open.
Stir in the celery leaves and serve with the sourdough bread for the juices.

recipes.title: Sole meunière with lemon thyme and sea purslane
recipes.why: Butter and lemon need a lean white with clean, high acidity.
steps: Dust the sole in the plain flour and fry in half the butter for 3–4 minutes per side.
Add the rest of the butter, let it turn nut-brown, then add the lemon juice, lemon thyme, sea purslane and parsley.
Spoon the butter over the fish and serve.

recipes.title: Razor clams with garlic, chilli and fennel pollen
recipes.why: Briny clams and garlic want a crisp, neutral white with a mineral edge.
steps: Grill the razor clams on a very hot plancha for 1–2 minutes, until they open.
Warm the garlic and red chilli in the olive oil and spoon over the clams.
Finish with the fennel pollen, parsley and lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Trout with almonds, brown butter and horseradish
recipes.why: Horseradish gives a peppery bite that a spicy white loves.
steps: Fry the trout fillets skin-side down for 3 minutes, turn for 1 minute and keep warm.
Brown the butter with the flaked almonds, then add the lemon juice.
Serve the trout with the potatoes, spoon over the almond butter and grate the horseradish on top. Scatter with parsley.

recipes.title: Pike-perch with lentils, dill and caraway
recipes.why: Dill and earthy lentils suit a peppery, fresh white.
steps: Simmer the puy lentils with the carrot and caraway seeds for 20 minutes, drain and dress with the white wine vinegar.
Stir the dill into the creme fraiche.
Fry the pike-perch skin-side down in the butter until crisp.
Serve on the lentils with a spoonful of the dill cream.

recipes.title: Mussels with green curry and Thai basil
recipes.why: Green curry's herbs and gentle heat want a peppery white with good acidity.
steps: Fry the green curry paste for 1 minute, then add the coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add the mussels, cover and cook for 4–5 minutes until open.
Stir in the lime juice and thai basil and scatter with spring onions.

recipes.title: Fish cakes with curried celeriac remoulade
recipes.why: Curry spice and celeriac's crunch suit a white with a peppery edge.
steps: Mix the cod, potatoes and parsley, season and shape into 8 cakes. Coat in the breadcrumbs.
Fry in the sunflower oil for 3 minutes per side, until golden.
Toss the celeriac with the mayonnaise and curry powder and serve alongside.

recipes.title: Grilled prawns with romesco
recipes.why: Roasted pepper and almond sauce match a fruity, dry rosé.
steps: Blitz the roasted red peppers, flaked almonds, garlic, smoked paprika, sherry vinegar and olive oil into a coarse romesco.
Grill the king prawns over high heat for 2 minutes per side.
Serve with the romesco for dipping.

recipes.title: Bouillabaisse-style fish stew with rouille
recipes.why: Saffron, fennel and tomato are the classic match for a rosé.
steps: Soften the fennel and two cloves of garlic in the olive oil, add the pastis, tomatoes, saffron and orange zest with 500 ml water and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the monkfish and cook for 5 minutes, then add the mussels and cook until they open.
Grate the remaining garlic into the mayonnaise for a quick rouille.
Serve the stew with the sourdough bread spread with rouille.

recipes.title: Salmon tartare with watermelon radish and shiso
recipes.why: Shiso's minty, floral note pairs with the red-fruit side of a pale rosé.
steps: Mix the salmon with the light soy sauce, lime juice and sesame oil.
Spoon into rings and top with the watermelon radish slices and shiso leaves.

recipes.title: Squid a la plancha with black olive and orange
recipes.why: Orange and olive bring the sun-dried fruit side of a rosé.
steps: Toss the fennel with the orange segments, black olives and half the olive oil.
Grill the squid on a very hot plancha for 1–2 minutes per side.
Slice and serve on the salad with parsley.

recipes.title: Seared tuna with cherry tomatoes and lovage
recipes.why: Meaty tuna and tomato suit a light, fruity red served cool.
steps: Toss the cherry tomatoes with the capers, red wine vinegar, half the olive oil and the lovage.
Rub the tuna steaks with oil and sear for 1 minute per side so the centre stays pink.
Slice and serve on the tomatoes.

recipes.title: Salmon with beetroot and horseradish crème fraîche
recipes.why: Earthy beetroot and salmon's richness need a light, juicy red.
steps: Roast the beetroot with the olive oil at 200 °C for 40 minutes.
Add the salmon fillets to the tray for the last 12 minutes.
Mix the horseradish into the creme fraiche and serve with dill.

recipes.title: Seared tuna with soy, shiitake and sansho pepper
recipes.why: Umami-rich tuna and mushrooms stand up to a light red.
steps: Fry the shiitake mushrooms in the sesame oil until golden, then add the fresh ginger, light soy sauce and mirin.
Sear the tuna steaks for 1 minute per side.
Slice, dust with the sansho pepper and serve over the mushrooms with spring onions.

recipes.title: Salmon with red wine butter and mushrooms
recipes.why: Red wine sauce and mushrooms make salmon a natural partner for a light red.
steps: Reduce the red wine with the shallot and thyme to about 3 tablespoons, then whisk in two-thirds of the butter.
Fry the chestnut mushrooms in the rest of the butter.
Sear the salmon fillets skin-side down for 5 minutes, turn for 1 minute and serve with the mushrooms and sauce.

recipes.title: Cedar-planked salmon with maple and mustard
recipes.why: Smoke from the plank and a sweet glaze suit a red with some oak.
steps: Mix the maple syrup and wholegrain mustard.
Lay the salmon on the soaked cedar plank and brush with the glaze.
Grill with the lid closed over medium heat for 20–25 minutes, until just cooked. Squeeze the lemon over.

recipes.title: Monkfish wrapped in prosciutto with juniper and lentils
recipes.why: Cured ham and earthy lentils give enough savoury depth for an oaked red.
steps: Simmer the puy lentils for 20 minutes, add the red wine and reduce until absorbed.
Lay the sage and juniper berries on the monkfish, wrap in prosciutto and sear in the olive oil.
Roast at 200 °C for 12–15 minutes, rest and slice. Serve on the lentils.

recipes.title: Tuna with caponata
recipes.why: Sweet-sour aubergine and meaty tuna suit a supple, fruity red.
steps: Fry the aubergines in the olive oil until golden. Add the celery, tomatoes, raisins and capers and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the red wine vinegar and caster sugar and cook for 2 minutes more.
Sear the tuna steaks for 1 minute per side and serve on the caponata.

recipes.title: Lobster salad with mango and lime
recipes.why: Tropical fruit and sweet lobster want a floral, dry white.
steps: Slice the lobster meat.
Toss the mango, avocado, lime juice and olive oil and season.
Top with the lobster and coriander leaves.

recipes.title: Scallops with cauliflower, raisins and curry oil
recipes.why: Mild curry spice and raisins match a fragrant, dry white.
steps: Simmer the cauliflower in the milk until soft and blend smooth.
Warm the sunflower oil with the curry powder for 2 minutes and strain.
Sear the scallops for 90 seconds per side. Serve on the purée with the golden raisins and curry oil.

recipes.title: Thai red curry with prawns and pineapple
recipes.why: Chilli heat and pineapple need an aromatic, slightly sweet white.
steps: Fry the red curry paste for 1 minute, add the coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the pineapple and king prawns and cook for 3 minutes. Season with the fish sauce.
Serve over jasmine rice with thai basil.

recipes.title: Duck-fat fried fish with lychee and chilli salsa
recipes.why: Lychee's perfume mirrors an aromatic white; the chilli wants its sweetness.
steps: Mix the lychees, red chilli, lime juice and coriander leaves.
Dust the sea bass in the rice flour and fry skin-side down in the sunflower oil until crisp.
Serve topped with the lychee salsa.

recipes.title: Langoustines with lemon verbena butter
recipes.why: Sweet langoustines and verbena match the perfume of an aromatic white.
steps: Mash the butter with the lemon verbena and a squeeze of lemon.
Spread over the langoustines and grill for 3–4 minutes until just opaque.

recipes.title: Cured trout with apple, cucumber and elderflower
recipes.why: Elderflower and apple suit a floral, crisp white.
steps: Cover the trout fillets in the caster sugar and sea salt for 2 hours, then rinse and pat dry.
Toss the green apple and cucumber with the elderflower cordial.
Slice the trout thinly and serve with the apple and cucumber and dill.

recipes.title: Octopus with potatoes and paprika
recipes.why: Smoked paprika and olive oil match a crisp, fruity Albariño.
steps: Simmer the octopus for 50–60 minutes, until tender. Cook the potatoes in the same water.
Slice the octopus and potatoes onto a wooden board.
Drizzle with the olive oil and sprinkle with smoked paprika and flaky salt.

recipes.title: Clams with white beans and chorizo
recipes.why: Briny clams and smoky chorizo want a crisp white with fruit.
steps: Fry the chorizo in the olive oil until it releases its fat, then add the garlic.
Add the white beans, dry white wine and clams, cover and cook until the clams open.
Finish with parsley.

recipes.title: Crab linguine with chilli, lemon and fennel seed
recipes.why: Sweet crab and lemon want a round white with gentle aromatics.
steps: Cook the linguine until al dente.
Warm the garlic, red chilli and fennel seeds in the olive oil, then add the crab meat and lemon zest and juice.
Toss with the linguine and a splash of cooking water and finish with parsley.

recipes.title: Sea bass with fennel, Pernod and cream
recipes.why: Aniseed and cream need a round, aromatic white.
steps: Soften the fennel in the butter for 10 minutes. Add the pastis and let it bubble.
Stir in the double cream and season.
Sear the sea bass skin-side down until crisp and serve on the fennel.

recipes.title: Scallops with Jerusalem artichoke, brown butter and sage
recipes.why: Brown butter and nutty artichoke match a toasty, oaked white.
steps: Simmer the jerusalem artichokes in the milk until soft and blend smooth.
Sear the scallops for 90 seconds per side.
Brown the butter with the sage leaves until crisp, add the lemon juice and spoon over the scallops on the purée.

recipes.title: Prawn risotto with lemongrass
recipes.why: A creamy risotto needs a round, barrel-aged white.
steps: Soften the shallot in half the butter, add the arborio rice and lemongrass and toast for 1 minute. Add the dry white wine.
Add the chicken stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 minutes.
Add the king prawns for the last 3 minutes, then remove the lemongrass and beat in the rest of the butter and the parmesan.

recipes.title: Smoked eel with beetroot and horseradish
recipes.why: Smoky, rich eel needs a crisp white with a touch of oak.
steps: Arrange the beetroot and smoked eel on plates.
Mix the horseradish into the creme fraiche and spoon alongside. Finish with dill.

recipes.title: Cod with smoked butter and samphire
recipes.why: Smoked butter echoes the toast of a lightly oaked white.
steps: Roast the cod at 200 °C for 10–12 minutes.
Blanch the samphire for 1 minute.
Melt the smoked butter with a squeeze of lemon and spoon over the fish and samphire.

recipes.title: Fish tacos with lime slaw and chipotle cream
recipes.why: Crisp fish, lime and cabbage want a zesty, neutral white.
steps: Toss the red cabbage with the juice of one lime and salt.
Dust the cod in the plain flour and fry in the sunflower oil until crisp.
Stir the chipotle in adobo into the sour cream and fill the warm corn tortillas with fish, slaw and chipotle cream.

recipes.title: Steamed clams with sake, butter and shiso
recipes.why: Clean, briny clams match a lean white with mineral acidity.
steps: Warm the garlic in the butter, add the clams and sake, cover and steam until open.
Scatter with the shiso leaves and serve with the broth.

recipes.title: Smoked salmon blinis with crème fraîche and caraway
recipes.why: Smoked salmon and cream are a classic for sparkling wine.
steps: Warm the blinis.
Top each with creme fraiche, a fold of smoked salmon, caraway seeds and dill.

recipes.title: Crab croquettes with saffron mayonnaise
recipes.why: Crisp croquettes want the bubbles and acidity of a sparkling wine.
steps: Cook the butter and plain flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk to a thick béchamel. Fold in the crab meat and chill.
Shape into small logs, dip in the eggs and roll in the breadcrumbs.
Fry in the sunflower oil at 180 °C until golden. Mix the saffron into the mayonnaise to serve.

recipes.title: Grilled red mullet with tapenade and fennel seed
recipes.why: Olive and tomato call for a dry rosé.
steps: Grill the red mullet skin-side up for 3–4 minutes.
Toss the cherry tomatoes with the olive oil and fennel seeds.
Serve the fish with the tomatoes and a spoonful of tapenade.

recipes.title: Salmon teriyaki with sesame greens
recipes.why: A sweet soy glaze and salmon suit a light, fruity red or a fragrant white.
steps: Simmer the light soy sauce, mirin and honey until syrupy.
Sear the salmon fillets, then brush with the glaze for the last minute.
Steam the pak choi and serve with the salmon, scattered with toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Roast cod with red wine lentils and smoked paprika
recipes.why: Red wine and pancetta make cod a match for a light, high-acid red.
steps: Fry the pancetta and shallot until golden, add the puy lentils, red wine and thyme and simmer with water until tender.
Dust the cod with the smoked paprika and roast at 200 °C for 10–12 minutes.
Serve the cod on the lentils.

recipes.title: Crab cakes with lemongrass and sweet chilli
recipes.why: Sweet chilli sauce wants a touch of sweetness and bright acidity.
steps: Mix the crab meat, breadcrumbs, eggs and lemongrass and shape into 8 cakes.
Fry in the sunflower oil for 3 minutes per side.
Serve with the sweet chilli sauce and lime.

recipes.title: Scallops with pork belly and apple purée
recipes.why: Sweet apple, rich pork and scallop suit an off-dry white.
steps: Roast the pork belly at 160 °C for 2 hours, then at 220 °C for 20 minutes to crackle. Cut into 8 pieces.
Cook the apples with the butter and cider vinegar until soft and blend.
Sear the scallops and serve with the pork belly and apple purée.

recipes.title: Prawn and pomelo salad with lime leaf
recipes.why: Floral lime leaf and juicy pomelo suit an aromatic white.
steps: Poach the king prawns for 2 minutes and cool.
Mix the fish sauce, lime juice and palm sugar.
Toss with the pomelo and kaffir lime leaves and finish with the toasted coconut.

recipes.title: Asparagus and smoked trout with soft egg
recipes.why: Asparagus, egg and smoke suit a peppery white.
steps: Boil the eggs for 6½ minutes and peel. Blanch the green asparagus for 2 minutes.
Arrange the asparagus with flaked smoked trout and halved eggs.
Drizzle with olive oil, finish with white pepper and chives.

recipes.title: Gurnard with mussel and saffron broth
recipes.why: A gently aromatic broth suits a round, fresh white.
steps: Soften the fennel in the olive oil, add the dry white wine and mussels and cook until open.
Add the saffron and 200 ml water and bring to a simmer.
Poach the gurnard in the broth for 5 minutes and serve in bowls.

recipes.title: Swordfish with salmoriglio
recipes.why: Meaty swordfish and herby lemon dressing can take a light, fresh red.
steps: Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, dried oregano and parsley.
Grill the swordfish steaks for 3 minutes per side.
Spoon the salmoriglio over the hot fish.

recipes.title: Pea and lovage soup
recipes.why: Lovage's celery-like spice suits a peppery, green-edged white.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter for 8 minutes.
Add the vegetable stock and peas and simmer for 5 minutes, then add the lovage and blend smooth.
Serve with a spoonful of creme fraiche.

recipes.title: Warm goat's cheese with beetroot and caraway
recipes.why: Tangy goat's cheese loves a lean, high-acid white; caraway adds a savoury lift.
steps: Roast the beetroot with half the olive oil and the caraway seeds at 200 °C for 40 minutes.
Grill the goat's cheese rounds until golden on top.
Dress the rocket with the red wine vinegar and the rest of the oil and serve with the beetroot and cheese.

recipes.title: Asparagus with blood orange hollandaise
recipes.why: Blood orange gives the sauce a bright, floral tang made for a racy white.
steps: Reduce the blood orange juice to 2 tablespoons.
Whisk the egg yolks with the reduced juice over a pan of barely simmering water until thick, then slowly whisk in the butter. Add the zest.
Simmer the white asparagus for 8–10 minutes until tender and serve with the sauce.

recipes.title: Wild mushroom toast with tarragon cream
recipes.why: Earthy mushrooms and cream need a rounded, oaked white; tarragon lifts it.
steps: Fry the wild mushrooms in the butter over high heat until golden, adding the garlic at the end.
Add the double cream and tarragon and bubble for 1 minute.
Spoon onto the toasted sourdough bread.

recipes.title: Chicken liver pâté with allspice and cherries
recipes.why: Allspice and cherry pull rich liver toward a bright, light red.
steps: Soften the shallot in a little butter, add the chicken livers and fry for 2–3 minutes so they stay pink inside.
Add the brandy and allspice, then blend with the rest of the butter until smooth. Chill in a dish for 4 hours.
Serve with the sour cherries and toasted sourdough bread.

recipes.title: Tomato bruschetta with wild fennel
recipes.why: Ripe tomato needs a high-acid red; fennel seed adds its herbal edge.
steps: Grill the sourdough bread and rub with the garlic.
Toss the tomatoes with the olive oil, fennel seeds and salt.
Pile onto the toast and finish with basil.

recipes.title: Gazpacho with smoked paprika oil
recipes.why: Cold tomato and pepper soup with a smoky oil wants a dry, savoury rosé.
steps: Blend the tomatoes, cucumber, red pepper, garlic, sherry vinegar and two-thirds of the olive oil until smooth. Season and chill.
Warm the rest of the olive oil with the smoked paprika for 1 minute.
Serve the gazpacho cold with a drizzle of the paprika oil.

recipes.title: Melon and jamón with mint and Espelette pepper
recipes.why: Sweet melon and salty ham suit a fruity rosé; Espelette adds gentle warmth.
steps: Arrange the cantaloupe melon and jamón on a platter.
Drizzle with olive oil and finish with mint and espelette pepper.

recipes.title: Leek and potato soup with smoked mussels
recipes.why: Smoked mussels give a creamy soup the depth for a round, fresh white.
steps: Soften the leeks in the butter for 10 minutes.
Add the potatoes and vegetable stock and simmer for 20 minutes, then blend.
Serve topped with the smoked mussels and chives.

recipes.title: Comté gougères with nutmeg
recipes.why: Warm cheese puffs are a classic with sparkling wine; nutmeg adds a soft spice.
steps: Bring the water and butter to a boil, add the plain flour and beat until the dough leaves the pan.
Off the heat, beat in the eggs one at a time, then the comte and nutmeg.
Pipe small mounds onto a lined tray and bake at 200 °C for 20–25 minutes, until puffed and golden.

recipes.title: Melon and cucumber salad with rose water
recipes.why: Rose water echoes the perfume of a dry white.
steps: Toss the cantaloupe melon and cucumber with the lime juice and rose water.
Scatter with crumbled feta and mint.

recipes.title: Carrot, ginger and coconut soup with lime leaf
recipes.why: Ginger and lime leaf need an aromatic, off-dry white.
steps: Soften the onion and fresh ginger, then add the carrots, vegetable stock and kaffir lime leaves and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove the leaves, add the coconut milk and blend smooth.

recipes.title: Prawn summer rolls with peanut-chilli dip
recipes.why: Herbs, chilli and sweet peanut sauce suit an off-dry white.
steps: Soften the rice paper in warm water one sheet at a time.
Fill with king prawns, rice noodles, thai basil and mint and roll tightly.
Whisk the peanut butter, sweet chilli sauce and lime juice with a splash of water for dipping.

recipes.title: Courgette carpaccio with lemon balm and pecorino
recipes.why: Lemon balm gives raw courgette a floral, citrus lift for a fresh white.
steps: Lay the courgette ribbons on plates.
Dress with lemon juice and olive oil, then scatter with the pecorino and lemon balm.

recipes.title: Celeriac soup with apple and celery salt
recipes.why: Celeriac and apple want a lean, crisp white with little fruit.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter, add the celeriac, apple and vegetable stock and simmer for 25 minutes.
Blend smooth and serve sprinkled with the celery seeds.

recipes.title: Pumpkin soup with Styrian pumpkin seed oil
recipes.why: Toasty pumpkin seed oil and sweet squash suit a peppery Austrian white.
steps: Roast the pumpkin and onion at 200 °C for 25 minutes.
Blend with the vegetable stock and season with the white pepper.
Serve with creme fraiche and a swirl of pumpkin seed oil.

recipes.title: Duck rillettes with pickled cherries
recipes.why: Pickled cherries lift rich duck toward a supple, fresh red.
steps: Salt the duck legs overnight, then rinse and cook in the duck fat with thyme and garlic at 140 °C for 3 hours.
Shred the meat with two forks, mixing in some of the fat, and pack into jars.
Serve with the pickled cherries and toasted sourdough bread.

recipes.title: Mushroom pâté with smoked garlic
recipes.why: Smoked garlic adds the toasty depth an oaked red likes.
steps: Fry the chestnut mushrooms in the butter with the smoked garlic and thyme until all the liquid evaporates.
Blend with the cream cheese until smooth and chill.
Serve with the toasted sourdough bread.

recipes.title: Burrata with roasted strawberries and black pepper
recipes.why: Roasted strawberry and pepper match a juicy, light red.
steps: Roast the strawberries with the balsamic vinegar at 200 °C for 12 minutes.
Tear the burrata onto plates and spoon over the strawberries and juices.
Finish with olive oil, black pepper and basil.

recipes.title: Grilled halloumi with peach and za'atar
recipes.why: Salty cheese and juicy peach suit a fruity rosé; za'atar adds herbal spice.
steps: Grill the halloumi and peaches until charred.
Drizzle with honey, lemon juice and olive oil and sprinkle with the zaatar.

recipes.title: Chilled cucumber soup with green apple and elderflower
recipes.why: Elderflower and apple make it fragrant enough for a floral white.
steps: Blend the cucumber, green apple, greek yoghurt and elderflower cordial until smooth. Season and chill.
Serve topped with dill.

recipes.title: Cauliflower velouté with smoked almonds
recipes.why: Creamy cauliflower and smoky almonds suit a toasty, oaked white.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter, add the cauliflower, milk and vegetable stock and simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend smooth and serve topped with the smoked almonds.

recipes.title: Celeriac remoulade with smoked ham
recipes.why: Smoked ham and mustard want a crisp white with a touch of oak.
steps: Toss the celeriac with the mayonnaise, dijon mustard and lemon juice.
Serve with the smoked ham and parsley.

recipes.title: Spring vegetable salad with lemon thyme
recipes.why: Peas and broad beans with lemon thyme suit a round, gently aromatic white.
steps: Blanch the peas, broad beans and green asparagus for 2 minutes and cool.
Dress with lemon juice, olive oil and lemon thyme.
Serve with spoonfuls of ricotta.

recipes.title: Tuscan bean soup with cavolo nero and fennel seed
recipes.why: Beans and bitter greens want a savoury, high-acid red.
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and fennel seeds in the olive oil.
Add the tomatoes, cannellini beans and 800 ml water and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the cavolo nero and cook for 10 minutes more. Serve with parmesan.

recipes.title: Tuscan chicken liver crostini with juniper
recipes.why: Juniper and rich liver suit a spicy, fresh red.
steps: Fry the chicken livers in the olive oil for 3 minutes with the juniper berries.
Add the red wine, anchovies and capers and cook for 2 minutes, then chop finely.
Spread on the toasted sourdough bread.

recipes.title: Beef carpaccio with smoked salt and rocket
recipes.why: Smoked salt gives raw beef the savoury depth for a medium, fresh red.
steps: Slice the beef fillet paper-thin and lay on plates.
Top with rocket and parmesan.
Drizzle with lemon juice and olive oil and sprinkle with the smoked salt.

recipes.title: Lamb meatballs with ras el hanout and yoghurt
recipes.why: Warm spices and lamb call for a spicy, fruity red.
steps: Mix the lamb mince with the ras el hanout, garlic and salt and roll into small balls.
Fry in the olive oil until browned and cooked through.
Serve with the greek yoghurt and mint.

recipes.title: Pork rillettes with cornichons and quatre épices
recipes.why: Warm spice and rich pork suit a supple red with good acidity.
steps: Cook the pork belly with the quatre epices, garlic, bay leaves and 200 ml water, covered, at 140 °C for 4 hours.
Shred with two forks, mixing in the fat, season and pack into jars.
Serve with cornichons and sourdough bread.

recipes.title: Tomato tarte fine with anchovies and herbes de Provence
recipes.why: Tomato, olive oil and herbs are the classic for a rosé.
steps: Lay the puff pastry on a tray and prick all over.
Cover with the tomatoes, add the anchovies, drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with the herbes de provence.
Bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes.

recipes.title: Comté soufflé with mace
recipes.why: A light, cheesy soufflé is made for the bubbles of a dry sparkling wine.
steps: Cook the butter and plain flour, whisk in the milk to a thick sauce, then beat in the yolks of the eggs, the comte and the ground mace.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks and fold in.
Spoon into buttered ramekins and bake at 200 °C for 12–14 minutes.

recipes.title: Grilled peach, mozzarella and lavender
recipes.why: Lavender gives the peach a floral note that a dry white echoes.
steps: Grill the peaches until charred.
Warm the honey with the dried lavender.
Serve the peaches with torn mozzarella, drizzled with lavender honey and olive oil.

recipes.title: Vietnamese chicken salad with lime leaf and chilli
recipes.why: Chilli and lime leaf call for a touch of sweetness and lots of acidity.
steps: Poach the chicken breast for 12 minutes, cool and shred.
Dissolve the palm sugar in the lime juice and fish sauce, add the red chilli.
Toss with the white cabbage, carrot, chicken and kaffir lime leaves. Finish with roasted peanuts.

recipes.title: Duck spring rolls with five spice and plum sauce
recipes.why: Five spice and sweet plum suit an aromatic, off-dry white.
steps: Mix the duck with the five spice and spring onions.
Roll into the spring roll wrappers and fry in the sunflower oil at 180 °C until crisp.
Serve with the plum sauce.

recipes.title: Avocado and grapefruit salad with coriander seed
recipes.why: Grapefruit and coriander seed suit a zesty, fruity white.
steps: Slice the avocado and arrange with the grapefruit and red onion.
Dress with olive oil and lime juice and scatter with the coriander seeds.

recipes.title: Fresh goat's cheese with radishes and nigella seeds
recipes.why: Tangy goat's cheese and peppery radish want a lean, crisp white.
steps: Spread the goat's cheese on a plate and top with the radishes.
Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with nigella seeds and flaky salt and serve with sourdough bread.

recipes.title: Sweetcorn velouté with smoked butter
recipes.why: Sweet corn and smoky butter mirror a buttery, oaked white.
steps: Soften the onion in half the smoked butter, add the sweetcorn, vegetable stock and milk and simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend smooth and pass through a sieve. Serve with the rest of the butter melted on top.

recipes.title: Mushroom and Gruyère tart with juniper
recipes.why: Earthy mushrooms and a hint of juniper suit a light, high-acid red.
steps: Fry the chestnut mushrooms in the butter with the thyme and juniper berries until golden.
Spread over the puff pastry, leaving a border, and scatter with the gruyere.
Bake at 200 °C for 25–30 minutes.

recipes.title: Heirloom tomato salad with strawberries and raspberry vinegar
recipes.why: Raspberry vinegar pulls ripe tomato toward a juicy, fruity red.
steps: Arrange the tomatoes and strawberries on a platter.
Dress with the raspberry vinegar and olive oil and finish with basil and flaky salt.

recipes.title: Jerusalem artichoke soup with toasted buckwheat
recipes.why: Nutty artichoke and toasted buckwheat suit a round white with a little weight.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter, add the jerusalem artichokes and vegetable stock and simmer for 25 minutes.
Blend smooth and serve with creme fraiche and the toasted buckwheat on top.

recipes.title: White asparagus with ham and wild garlic
recipes.why: Wild garlic's pungency matches a peppery, fresh white.
steps: Simmer the white asparagus and potatoes until tender.
Blend the wild garlic with the olive oil and lemon juice.
Serve with the cooked ham and the wild garlic oil.

recipes.title: Courgette and mint fritters with sumac yoghurt
recipes.why: Fried fritters and tangy sumac suit a crisp, fruity rosé.
steps: Mix the courgette, feta, eggs, plain flour and mint.
Fry spoonfuls in the olive oil for 2–3 minutes per side.
Stir the sumac into the greek yoghurt and serve alongside.

recipes.title: Kohlrabi and apple salad with lemongrass
recipes.why: Lemongrass gives crisp kohlrabi a floral lift for a racy white.
steps: Whisk the lime juice, honey, olive oil and lemongrass.
Toss with the kohlrabi and green apple.

recipes.title: Aubergine involtini with ricotta and fennel seed
recipes.why: Tomato and ricotta want a bright, high-acid Italian red.
steps: Grill the aubergines brushed with olive oil.
Roll each slice around a spoonful of ricotta mixed with basil and lay in a dish on the passata.
Sprinkle with the fennel seeds and bake at 190 °C for 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Pappa al pomodoro with black pepper and pecorino
recipes.why: Tomato, bread and pepper suit a spicy, high-acid red.
steps: Soften the garlic in the olive oil, add the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the sourdough bread and 300 ml water and cook until thick.
Serve with black pepper, pecorino and basil.

recipes.title: Pear, fennel and elderflower salad with pecorino
recipes.why: Elderflower and pear echo the perfume of a dry, aromatic white.
steps: Whisk the elderflower cordial, lemon juice and olive oil.
Toss with the pear, fennel and rocket and top with the pecorino.

recipes.title: Peach and burrata with rose and pistachio
recipes.why: Rose water and ripe peach mirror a floral, fruit-rich white.
steps: Toss the peaches with the rose water and honey.
Arrange around the torn burrata, drizzle with olive oil and scatter with pistachios.

recipes.title: Chicken and almond pastilla triangles with orange blossom
recipes.why: Orange blossom, cinnamon and sweet almond suit an aromatic, dry white.
steps: Soften the onion, add the chicken, flaked almonds, cinnamon and orange blossom water and season.
Cut the filo pastry into strips, brush with butter, fill and fold into triangles.
Bake at 190 °C for 20 minutes and dust with the caster sugar and a little more cinnamon.

recipes.title: Carrot and orange soup with coriander seed and orange blossom
recipes.why: Coriander seed and orange blossom make the soup floral enough for a white.
steps: Soften the onion and coriander seeds in the olive oil, add the carrots and vegetable stock and simmer for 25 minutes.
Blend with the orange zest and juice, then stir in the orange blossom water.

recipes.title: Prawn and lychee salad with jasmine tea dressing
recipes.why: Jasmine and lychee reach the perfume of a floral, dry white.
steps: Poach the king prawns for 2 minutes and cool.
Whisk the jasmine tea, lime juice and honey.
Toss with the lychees, cucumber, prawns and mint.

recipes.title: Spiced pumpkin samosas with cardamom and mango chutney
recipes.why: Cardamom and sweet chutney suit a perfumed, spicy white.
steps: Mash the pumpkin with the peas, cardamom, cumin seeds and fresh ginger.
Fill strips of filo pastry and fold into triangles.
Fry in the sunflower oil at 180 °C until crisp and serve with the mango chutney.

recipes.title: Roast carrot dip with rose harissa
recipes.why: Rose harissa's floral heat is made for an aromatic white.
steps: Roast the carrots and garlic with the olive oil at 200 °C for 30 minutes.
Blend with the greek yoghurt and rose harissa.
Serve with warm flatbread.

recipes.title: Onion and Munster tart with cumin
recipes.why: Pungent Munster and cumin are a classic match for an aromatic white.
steps: Cook the onion slowly in the butter for 30 minutes until golden.
Line a tin with the puff pastry, add the onion and munster and pour over the eggs beaten with the double cream.
Sprinkle with cumin seeds and bake at 190 °C for 25 minutes.

recipes.title: Duck and lychee salad with star anise
recipes.why: Lychee and star anise bring out the spice and perfume of an aromatic white.
steps: Rub the duck breast with the ground star anise and cook skin-side down for 10 minutes, then 3 minutes on the other side. Rest and slice.
Mix the light soy sauce and honey.
Toss the little gem lettuce with the lychees and dressing and top with the duck and spring onions.

recipes.title: Green papaya salad with tamarind and chilli
recipes.why: Tamarind's sweet sourness and chilli heat want an off-dry, racy white.
steps: Pound the red chilli with the palm sugar, then mix with the tamarind paste, fish sauce and lime juice.
Toss with the green papaya and cherry tomatoes and top with roasted peanuts.

recipes.title: Pork larb with lemongrass and mint
recipes.why: Lime, chilli and herbs need an off-dry white with bright acidity.
steps: Fry the pork mince with the lemongrass until cooked through.
Season with the fish sauce, lime juice and red chilli and stir in the mint.
Serve in the little gem lettuce leaves.

recipes.title: Smoked trout with star anise pickled pear
recipes.why: Sweet pickled pear and smoky fish suit an off-dry, high-acid white.
steps: Warm the cider vinegar with the caster sugar and star anise, pour over the pear and leave for 20 minutes.
Mix the horseradish into the creme fraiche.
Serve the smoked trout with the pickled pear, cream and dill.

recipes.title: Watermelon gazpacho with chilli and lemongrass
recipes.why: Sweet watermelon and chilli heat call for an off-dry white.
steps: Blend the watermelon, tomatoes, cucumber, red chilli, lemongrass and lime juice until smooth and chill.
Serve with a drizzle of olive oil and mint.

recipes.title: Smoked duck breast with blackberries and hazelnuts
recipes.why: Smoky duck and dark berries suit a red with some oak.
steps: Arrange the smoked duck breast with the rocket and blackberries.
Dress with balsamic vinegar and olive oil and scatter with hazelnuts.

recipes.title: Grilled quail with pomegranate molasses
recipes.why: Sweet-sour pomegranate and charred quail suit a juicy, oaked red.
steps: Marinate the quail in the pomegranate molasses, garlic and olive oil for 1 hour.
Grill for 5–6 minutes per side.
Scatter with pomegranate seeds and parsley.

recipes.title: Beetroot tarte tatin with goat's cheese and smoked salt
recipes.why: Sweet, earthy beetroot and smoke suit an oaked red.
steps: Make a light caramel with the caster sugar and butter, add the balsamic vinegar and lay the beetroot in the pan.
Cover with the puff pastry and bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes.
Turn out and top with the goat's cheese and smoked salt.

recipes.title: Fennel sausage crostini with chilli
recipes.why: Fennel and chilli pick up the spice of a fresh red.
steps: Fry the sausage meat with the fennel seeds and red chilli until browned.
Spread the sourdough bread with ricotta and top with the sausage.

recipes.title: Grilled radicchio with anchovy and black pepper
recipes.why: Bitter radicchio and anchovy want a savoury, high-acid red.
steps: Grill the radicchio until charred.
Warm the anchovies and garlic in the olive oil until the anchovies melt.
Spoon over the radicchio with the balsamic vinegar and black pepper.

recipes.title: Vitello tonnato with celery leaf
recipes.why: A tuna-mayonnaise sauce and capers want a crisp, lean white.
steps: Poach the veal topside in salted water for 40 minutes and cool in the liquid.
Blend the tuna in oil, mayonnaise, anchovies and lemon juice to a smooth sauce.
Slice the veal thinly, spoon over the sauce and finish with capers and celery leaves.

recipes.title: Oeufs mayonnaise with tarragon and pickled shallots
recipes.why: Egg and tangy mayonnaise need a lean, high-acid white.
steps: Pickle the shallot in the white wine vinegar for 15 minutes.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and halve.
Spoon over the mayonnaise mixed with tarragon and top with the pickled shallot.

recipes.title: Beef tartare with violet mustard
recipes.why: Violet mustard gives raw beef a floral note that a red echoes.
steps: Mix the beef fillet with the violet mustard, shallot and capers and season.
Shape on plates with an egg yolk on top and serve with toasted sourdough bread.

recipes.title: Lamb kofta with rose harissa
recipes.why: Rose harissa's floral heat and lamb suit a perfumed, full-bodied red.
steps: Mix the lamb mince with the rose harissa and cumin seeds and shape onto skewers.
Grill for 8 minutes, turning.
Serve with flatbread, greek yoghurt and mint.

recipes.title: Carne cruda with lemon and dried rose
recipes.why: Raw beef and a hint of rose meet the floral perfume and grip of a firm red.
steps: Mix the beef fillet with the lemon juice, olive oil and garlic and season.
Shape on plates and finish with the parmesan and dried rose petals.

recipes.title: Beef and porcini agnolotti with sage butter
recipes.why: Roast meat, porcini and sage suit the tannin and lift of a firm red.
steps: Mix the beef chuck with the dried porcini and parmesan.
Roll the pasta dough thin, fill with small mounds and pinch into agnolotti.
Cook for 3 minutes and toss with the butter foamed with the sage leaves.

recipes.title: Beef empanadas with cumin and raisins
recipes.why: Spiced beef and raisins match the ripe dark fruit of a red.
steps: Fry the onion and beef mince with the cumin seeds and smoked paprika, then add the raisins and eggs.
Cut the shortcrust pastry into rounds, fill, fold and crimp.
Bake at 200 °C for 20–25 minutes.

recipes.title: Provoleta with plum jam and oregano
recipes.why: Melted cheese and dark fruit suit a ripe, plush red.
steps: Grill the provolone in a hot pan until crusty on both sides and soft inside.
Top with the plum jam, dried oregano, red chilli and olive oil and serve with bread.

recipes.title: Chorizo with dates and smoked paprika
recipes.why: Sweet dates and smoky chorizo match a jammy, low-acid red.
steps: Fry the chorizo until it releases its oil.
Add the medjool dates and smoked paprika for 2 minutes and finish with the sherry vinegar.

recipes.title: Lahmacun with pomegranate and sumac onions
recipes.why: Spiced lamb and pomegranate suit a fruity, spicy red.
steps: Mix the lamb mince with the tomato paste and allspice and spread thinly over the flatbread.
Bake at 230 °C for 8–10 minutes.
Top with the red onion tossed in sumac and the pomegranate seeds.

recipes.title: Merguez with rose harissa and mint yoghurt
recipes.why: Rose harissa's floral heat and spiced lamb suit a fruity red with spice.
steps: Grill the merguez for 8 minutes, turning.
Mix the greek yoghurt with mint and serve with the merguez, rose harissa and flatbread.

recipes.title: Lamb skewers with plum and smoked paprika
recipes.why: Ripe plum and smoke match a fruit-rich, oaked red.
steps: Toss the lamb leg with the smoked paprika, garlic and olive oil.
Thread onto skewers with the plums and grill for 8–10 minutes.

recipes.title: Venison carpaccio with juniper and cocoa nibs
recipes.why: Juniper and cocoa echo the spice and toast of a big, oaked red.
steps: Slice the venison loin paper-thin and lay on plates.
Drizzle with olive oil and scatter with juniper berries, cocoa nibs, blackberries and rocket.

recipes.title: Bresaola with smoked almonds and aged balsamic
recipes.why: Cured beef and smoky almonds stand up to a big, oaked, tannic red.
steps: Lay the bresaola on plates with the rocket and parmesan.
Scatter with the smoked almonds and drizzle with the balsamic vinegar.

recipes.title: Panzanella with celery leaf
recipes.why: Tomato and vinegar-soaked bread want a high-acid red.
steps: Chop the tomatoes and salt them for 10 minutes.
Toss with the sourdough bread, red onion, red wine vinegar and olive oil and leave for 15 minutes.
Finish with celery leaves and basil.

recipes.title: Asparagus and Gruyère puff tart
recipes.why: Crisp pastry and cheese are made for sparkling wine; lemon thyme keeps it fresh.
steps: Spread the puff pastry with the creme fraiche and scatter with the gruyere.
Lay the green asparagus on top and sprinkle with the lemon thyme.
Bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes.

recipes.title: Roast beetroot with orange and tarragon
recipes.why: Earthy beetroot and orange suit a light, juicy red; tarragon adds lift.
steps: Roast the beetroot at 200 °C for 45 minutes, peel and cut into wedges.
Toss with the orange, tarragon, olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Crumble the goat's cheese on top.

recipes.title: Pork and pistachio terrine with prunes
recipes.why: Prunes and pork suit a supple, fresh red.
steps: Mix the pork mince, chicken livers, pistachios, prunes, brandy and thyme and season well.
Line a terrine with the pancetta, fill and cover.
Bake in a water bath at 160 °C for 90 minutes, then press and chill overnight.

recipes.title: Beetroot and blackberry salad with goat's curd
recipes.why: Blackberries pull earthy beetroot toward the red fruit of a light red.
steps: Roast the beetroot, peel and slice.
Dress with olive oil and sherry vinegar and arrange with the blackberries and goat's cheese.
Scatter with hazelnuts.

recipes.title: Ajo blanco with white grapes
recipes.why: Cold almond and garlic soup with grapes suits a crisp, fruity white.
steps: Soak the sourdough bread in water, squeeze and blend with the blanched almonds, garlic, sherry vinegar, olive oil and 500 ml cold water.
Season and chill, then serve with the white grapes.

recipes.title: Endive, pear and walnut salad with elderflower dressing
recipes.why: Bitter endive and floral elderflower want a racy, aromatic white.
steps: Whisk the elderflower cordial, cider vinegar and olive oil.
Toss with the endive leaves and sliced pear and scatter with walnuts.

recipes.title: Leek and Gruyère quiche with nutmeg
recipes.why: Rich custard and cheese suit a round, oaked white.
steps: Blind-bake the shortcrust pastry in a tart tin.
Soften the leeks in the butter and spread over the pastry with the gruyere.
Pour over the eggs beaten with the double cream and nutmeg and bake at 180 °C for 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Salade niçoise with herbes de Provence
recipes.why: Tuna, olives and herbs are the classic for a rosé.
steps: Boil the potatoes, green beans and eggs.
Whisk the olive oil, red wine vinegar and herbes de provence.
Arrange everything with the tuna in oil, black olives and anchovies and dress.

recipes.title: Egg and chive salad with radish and white pepper
recipes.why: Egg, radish and white pepper suit a peppery, fresh white.
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and chop.
Mix with the mayonnaise, chives and white pepper.
Serve on rye bread with sliced radishes.

recipes.title: Chicken satay with galangal and peanut
recipes.why: Galangal and sweet peanut sauce suit a spicy, perfumed white.
steps: Marinate the chicken thighs with the galangal, light soy sauce and half the coconut milk.
Thread onto skewers and grill for 8 minutes.
Warm the peanut butter with the rest of the coconut milk, palm sugar and lime juice for dipping.

recipes.title: Fig and goat's cheese salad with lavender honey
recipes.why: Lavender and figs match the floral, fruit-rich side of a white.
steps: Warm the honey with the dried lavender.
Arrange the fresh figs, goat's cheese and rocket and drizzle with the lavender honey and olive oil.

recipes.title: Beef cheeks braised in Nebbiolo with dried rose
recipes.why: Wine-braised beef and a whisper of rose meet the tannin, acidity and perfume of a firm red.
steps: Brown the beef cheeks, then soften the onion and carrot in the same pot with the tomato paste.
Add the red wine and red wine vinegar, cover and braise at 150 °C for 3½ hours.
Reduce the sauce, add the dried rose petals and serve with soft polenta.

recipes.title: Tajarin with veal ragù and violet
recipes.why: A meat ragù with a floral edge suits the perfume and grip of a firm red.
steps: Brown the veal mince with the onion in the butter, add the red wine, tomatoes and violet mustard and simmer for 2 hours.
Cook the tagliatelle for 2 minutes and toss with the ragù.
Serve with parmesan.

recipes.title: Roast leg of lamb with anchovy, rosemary and lemon
recipes.why: Fatty lamb, lemon and herbs need the acidity and firm tannin of a structured red.
steps: Pound the anchovies, garlic, rosemary and lemon zest into a paste and push into slits in the lamb leg.
Roast on the potatoes at 180 °C for 80–90 minutes, basting with the lemon juice and olive oil.
Rest for 15 minutes before carving.

recipes.title: Steak au poivre
recipes.why: A black pepper crust and cognac cream suit a spicy, oaked, full red.
steps: Press the black pepper into both sides of the sirloin steak and sear in the butter for 3–4 minutes per side. Rest.
Flame the brandy in the pan, add the beef stock and double cream and reduce to a sauce.
Pour over the steaks.

recipes.title: Smoked brisket with coffee and pepper rub
recipes.why: Smoke, coffee and pepper match a big, spicy, oaked red.
steps: Rub the beef brisket with the black pepper, ground coffee, smoked paprika, light brown sugar and flaky salt.
Smoke at 120 °C for 8–10 hours, wrapping in paper when the bark sets, until very tender.
Rest for 1 hour and slice.

recipes.title: Chili con carne with chipotle and dark chocolate
recipes.why: Smoky chilli, cumin and cocoa want a spicy, fruit-rich, oaked red.
steps: Brown the beef chuck in the olive oil, then soften the onion with the cumin seeds.
Add the tomatoes, chipotle in adobo and 300 ml water and simmer for 2 hours.
Add the kidney beans and dark chocolate and cook for 20 minutes more.

recipes.title: Lamb shoulder with cumin, smoked paprika and garlic
recipes.why: Smoky spice and slow-roast lamb meet a peppery, oaked red.
steps: Rub the lamb shoulder with the cumin seeds, smoked paprika, garlic and olive oil.
Roast covered with the red wine at 160 °C for 4 hours, until it pulls apart.
Rest and shred with the juices.

recipes.title: Short ribs with black cherry glaze
recipes.why: Black cherry and smoky glaze match a ripe, fruit-forward, oaked red.
steps: Brown the beef short ribs, add the onion, garlic, red wine and 300 ml water and braise at 150 °C for 3 hours.
Reduce the braising liquid with the black cherry jam and smoked paprika to a glaze.
Brush the ribs with the glaze and char on a hot grill.

recipes.title: Beef fillet with blackberry and vanilla jus
recipes.why: Vanilla and blackberry echo the oak and ripe fruit of a plush red.
steps: Reduce the red wine with the vanilla pod, add the beef stock and reduce again, then add the blackberries.
Sear the beef fillet in the butter and roast at 200 °C for 15–18 minutes. Rest.
Serve sliced with roast potatoes and the jus.

recipes.title: Lamb tagine with prunes and cinnamon
recipes.why: Prunes and warm spice pull lamb toward a ripe, generous red.
steps: Brown the lamb shoulder, add the onion, cinnamon and ground ginger and cover with water.
Simmer for 2 hours, add the prunes and honey and cook for 20 minutes more.
Serve over couscous with flaked almonds.

recipes.title: Grilled flank steak with chimichurri
recipes.why: Charred beef and herby chimichurri are the classic for a red.
steps: Chop the parsley and mix with the dried oregano, garlic, red wine vinegar, chilli flakes and olive oil.
Grill the flank steak for 4–5 minutes per side and rest.
Slice against the grain and spoon over the chimichurri.

recipes.title: Asado-style beef ribs with salsa criolla
recipes.why: Fatty grilled ribs need the ripe fruit and soft tannin of a red.
steps: Salt the beef short ribs and grill slowly over embers for 2 hours, bone side down first.
Dice the red onion, red pepper and tomatoes and dress with the red wine vinegar and dried oregano.
Serve the ribs with the salsa criolla.

recipes.title: Beef and plum stew with star anise
recipes.why: Plums and star anise lift beef toward a ripe, dark-fruited red.
steps: Brown the beef chuck and onion, add the red wine, beef stock and star anise and simmer for 2 hours.
Add the plums and cook for 20 minutes more.

recipes.title: BBQ beef ribs with bourbon and molasses
recipes.why: Sweet, smoky glaze and rich beef suit a jammy, low-acid red.
steps: Wrap the beef short ribs in foil and cook at 150 °C for 3½ hours.
Simmer the molasses, bourbon, tomato paste, smoked paprika and cider vinegar to a glaze.
Brush over the ribs and grill until sticky.

recipes.title: Meatballs in sweet tomato sauce with raisins
recipes.why: A sweet, fruity tomato sauce suits a ripe, jammy red.
steps: Mix the beef mince, breadcrumbs and eggs, season and roll into balls. Brown in the olive oil.
Add the passata and raisins and simmer for 30 minutes.
Finish with basil and pine nuts.

recipes.title: Lamb burgers with fig chutney
recipes.why: Sweet fig and spiced lamb match a jammy, ripe red.
steps: Mix the lamb mince with the cumin seeds and shape into 4 burgers.
Grill for 4–5 minutes per side.
Serve in the burger buns with fig chutney, goat's cheese and rocket.

recipes.title: Lamb rump with lavender and honey
recipes.why: Lavender adds a floral note that a perfumed, full-bodied red echoes.
steps: Rub the lamb rump with the dried lavender, garlic and thyme.
Sear fat-side down, brush with honey and roast at 200 °C for 12–15 minutes.
Rest and serve with the green beans.

recipes.title: Venison with beetroot and violet mustard
recipes.why: Violet and earthy beetroot meet the floral side of a red.
steps: Roast the beetroot at 200 °C for 40 minutes.
Sear the venison loin in the butter and roast for 6 minutes. Rest.
Deglaze with the red wine, whisk in the violet mustard and serve with the beetroot.

recipes.title: Portuguese beef with red wine, bay and clove
recipes.why: Bay, clove and wine-braised beef suit a perfumed, structured red.
steps: Marinate the beef chuck overnight in the red wine with the bay leaves, cloves and garlic.
Brown in the olive oil, add the marinade and braise for 2 hours, adding the potatoes for the last 40 minutes.

recipes.title: Tomahawk steak with smoked bone marrow butter
recipes.why: Smoke, char and fat stand up to a big, oaked, tannic red.
steps: Roast the bone marrow and mash with the butter, rosemary and smoked salt.
Grill the tomahawk steak over indirect heat, then sear hard, to 54 °C inside.
Rest and serve with the marrow butter and black pepper.

recipes.title: Wagyu burger with smoked cheddar and onion jam
recipes.why: Smoky cheese and rich beef need a big, oaked red.
steps: Cook the onion slowly with the light brown sugar and balsamic vinegar until jammy.
Shape the beef mince into 4 patties and grill, adding the smoked cheddar at the end.
Serve in the burger buns with the onion jam.

recipes.title: Rib of beef with juniper and red wine shallots
recipes.why: Juniper and rich beef suit a powerful, tannic red.
steps: Rub the rib of beef with the juniper berries and black pepper and roast at 200 °C for 20 minutes, then 160 °C for 1 hour.
Braise the shallot in the butter and red wine until soft and glossy.
Rest the beef and carve.

recipes.title: Bistecca with rosemary and lemon
recipes.why: Charred beef and lemon want a tannic red with lively acidity.
steps: Grill the t-bone steak over embers for 6–7 minutes per side, standing it on the bone at the end.
Rest on the rosemary and slice.
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon and sprinkle with flaky salt.

recipes.title: Oxtail stew with allspice and capers
recipes.why: Rich oxtail and salty capers need a firm, savoury red.
steps: Brown the oxtail, add the onion, celery, anchovies, allspice, red wine and tomatoes and braise for 4 hours.
Stir in the capers and serve.

recipes.title: Duck confit with lentils and juniper
recipes.why: Rich confit and earthy lentils suit a tannic red from the southwest.
steps: Roast the duck legs at 200 °C for 25 minutes until crisp.
Fry the pancetta, add the puy lentils, juniper berries, thyme, red wine and water and simmer until tender.
Serve the duck on the lentils.

recipes.title: Cassoulet with Toulouse sausage and duck
recipes.why: Fat-rich beans and meats need a very tannic Tannat or Madiran.
steps: Simmer the white beans with the pancetta, garlic and cloves for 1 hour.
Brown the pork sausages and duck legs and layer with the beans and tomatoes.
Top with breadcrumbs and bake at 160 °C for 2 hours, breaking the crust twice.

recipes.title: Grilled lamb chops with anchovy and smoked paprika butter
recipes.why: Fatty lamb and salty butter tame a very tannic red.
steps: Mash the butter with the anchovies, smoked paprika, garlic and parsley.
Grill the lamb chops for 3 minutes per side.
Top with slices of the anchovy butter.

recipes.title: Beef shin ragù with pappardelle and cloves
recipes.why: A rich, slow ragù needs a dense, tannic red.
steps: Brown the beef shin, add the onion, red wine, tomatoes and cloves and braise for 4 hours until it falls apart.
Shred the meat into the sauce and toss with the cooked pappardelle.
Serve with parmesan.

recipes.title: Lamb shanks with rosemary and garlic
recipes.why: Slow-cooked lamb and rosemary suit a full, spicy red.
steps: Brown the lamb shanks, add the onion, garlic, rosemary, red wine and beef stock and braise for 3 hours.
Reduce the sauce and serve over mashed potatoes.

recipes.title: Moussaka with cinnamon
recipes.why: Spiced lamb and béchamel suit a full, spicy red.
steps: Brown the lamb mince with the cinnamon and add the tomatoes. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Make a béchamel with the butter, plain flour and milk.
Layer aubergines and lamb, top with béchamel and kefalotyri and bake at 180 °C for 45 minutes.

recipes.title: Hare ragù with juniper and chocolate
recipes.why: Gamey hare, juniper and cocoa need a full, spicy red.
steps: Marinate the hare in the red wine and juniper berries overnight.
Brown, add the onion and marinade and braise for 3 hours. Shred the meat.
Stir in the dark chocolate and toss with the pappardelle.

recipes.title: Steak frites with béarnaise
recipes.why: Steak and tarragon butter sauce suit a medium red with fresh acidity.
steps: Fry the potatoes twice in the sunflower oil, first at 150 °C then at 190 °C.
Whisk the egg yolks with the reduced white wine vinegar, then the melted butter, and add the tarragon.
Sear the sirloin steak and serve with the fries and béarnaise.

recipes.title: Beef bourguignon with orange zest
recipes.why: Wine-braised beef suits a medium red; orange zest brightens it.
steps: Brown the beef chuck and pancetta, add the red wine and thyme and braise for 2½ hours.
Add the shallot and chestnut mushrooms and cook for 30 minutes more.
Finish with the orange zest.

recipes.title: Calf's liver with sage and onions
recipes.why: Liver and sweet onions suit a medium, fresh red.
